title: Defer driver upgrades to shutdown using validated cached plans
description:
Phase 1 prevents packages with Modaliases, including those pulled in as dependencies, from being installed during normal unattended upgrades. This proposal adds the shutdown installation path for those deferred updates.

Normal runs resolve the deferred transaction, download and verify its archives, and save a versioned plan with an apply-on-shutdown marker. The existing shutdown service invokes a dedicated installation mode when that marker is present.

Before installation, the saved transaction is revalidated against current package state and policy, and cached archives are checked for trust, size and SHA256. Installation uses the validated package manager transaction without downloading missing archives. The plan is consumed only after all planned package versions are confirmed fully installed.

The change also protects deferred archives from normal unattended-upgrades cleanup, accepts shared dependencies already installed at their exact planned versions, and coordinates shutdown handoff and PID-file ownership.

Validation:
- Full test suite: 145 passed, 6 skipped, including lint and typing checks.
- Real dpkg installation test using an isolated package root.
- Debian binary package built successfully on Ubuntu 26.04 arm64.
- Real reboot test in a disposable Multipass VM: the ordinary update installed during the normal run, while the driver transaction remained deferred.
- With the test repository stopped, shutdown installed the cached driver transaction and completed a 45-second maintainer script despite SIGTERM requests after the 30-second inhibitor delay.
- After reboot, all test packages were fully installed at the expected versions and the saved plan had been removed.

The reboot test uses synthetic packages; it does not establish behavior for every real DKMS driver. Desktop UX and terminal notifications are not implemented yet.

@@ -0,0 +1,211 @@
+#!/usr/bin/python3
+
+import copy
+import os
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from contextlib import ExitStack, nullcontext
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import Mock, patch
+
+import unattended_upgrade as uu
+
+
+class TestDeferredDriverState(unittest.TestCase):
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.addCleanup(directory.cleanup)
+        self.rootdir = directory.name
+        self.plan_path = uu.deferred_driver_plan_path(self.rootdir)
+        self.apply_path = uu.deferred_driver_apply_marker_path(self.rootdir)
+        self.reboot_path = uu.reboot_required_path(self.rootdir)
+        root = dict(name="ordinary-root", architecture="all", version="2.0")
+        driver = dict(name="driver-dependency", architecture="all", version="2.0")
+        self.plan = dict(
+            version=uu.DEFERRED_DRIVER_UPGRADES_PLAN_VERSION,
+            roots=[root], packages=[driver, root], modaliases=[driver])
+        self.options = SimpleNamespace(
+            dry_run=False, download_only=False, verbose=False, debug=False)
+
+    def touch_marker(self, path):
+        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
+        with open(path, "w") as fp:
+            fp.write("existing requirement\n")
+
+    def existing_state(self):
+        uu.write_deferred_driver_plan(self.plan, self.rootdir)
+        self.touch_marker(self.apply_path)
+        self.touch_marker(self.reboot_path)
+
+    def contents(self, path):
+        with open(path, "rb") as fp:
+            return fp.read()
+
+    def prepare(self):
+        # Exercise the real publication code and file helpers. Resolution and
+        # archive acquisition have their own integration tests.
+        fetcher = Mock(RESULT_CONTINUE=0)
+        fetcher.run.return_value = 0
+        manager = Mock()
+        manager.get_archives.return_value = True
+        with ExitStack() as stack:
+            for name, value in (
+                    ("mark_pkgs_to_upgrade", Mock()),
+                    ("sanity_problem", Mock(return_value=None)),
+                    ("make_deferred_driver_plan", Mock(return_value=self.plan)),
+                    ("should_stop", Mock(return_value=False)),
+                    ("deferred_driver_archives_are_verified", Mock(return_value=True))):
+                stack.enter_context(patch.object(uu, name, value))
+            stack.enter_context(patch.object(
+                uu.apt_pkg, "Acquire", return_value=fetcher))
+            stack.enter_context(patch.object(uu.apt_pkg, "SourceList"))
+            stack.enter_context(patch.object(
+                uu.apt_pkg, "PackageManager", return_value=manager))
+            return uu.prepare_deferred_driver_upgrades(
+                Mock(), [SimpleNamespace(name="ordinary-root")], self.rootdir, False)
+
+    def run_without_installation(self):
+        with patch.object(uu.apt_pkg, "SystemLock", return_value=nullcontext()), \
+             patch.object(uu.apt_pkg, "config",
+                          SimpleNamespace(find_b=Mock(return_value=False))), \
+             patch.object(uu, "SIGNAL_STOP_REQUEST", False), \
+             patch.object(uu, "UnattendedUpgradesCache") as cache_class, \
+             patch.object(uu, "install_deferred_driver_plan") as install:
+            result = uu.run_deferred_driver_upgrades(
+                self.options, self.rootdir, "unused.log")
+            cache_class.assert_not_called()
+            install.assert_not_called()
+            return result
+
+    def test_reboot_marker_failure_does_not_publish_plan(self):
+        with patch.object(uu, "create_reboot_required_marker", side_effect=OSError):
+            self.assertFalse(self.prepare())
+
+        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(self.plan_path))
+        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(self.apply_path))
+
+    def test_reboot_marker_failure_preserves_existing_armed_plan(self):
+        self.existing_state()
+        old_plan = self.contents(self.plan_path)
+        old_apply = self.contents(self.apply_path)
+        replacement = copy.deepcopy(self.plan)
+        for key in ("roots", "packages", "modaliases"):
+            for entry in replacement[key]:
+                entry["version"] = "3.0"
+        self.plan = replacement
+
+        with patch.object(uu, "create_reboot_required_marker", side_effect=OSError):
+            self.assertFalse(self.prepare())
+
+        self.assertEqual(self.contents(self.plan_path), old_plan)
+        self.assertEqual(self.contents(self.apply_path), old_apply)
+
+    def test_plan_replacement_failure_does_not_arm_new_plan(self):
+        with patch.object(uu.os, "replace", side_effect=OSError):
+            self.assertFalse(self.prepare())
+
+        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(self.plan_path))
+        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(self.apply_path))
+        self.assertTrue(os.path.isfile(self.reboot_path))
+
+    def test_apply_marker_failure_keeps_prepared_plan_for_later_retry(self):
+        with patch.object(
+                uu, "create_deferred_driver_apply_marker", side_effect=OSError):
+            self.assertFalse(self.prepare())
+
+        self.assertEqual(uu.read_deferred_driver_plan(self.rootdir), self.plan)
+        self.assertTrue(os.path.isfile(self.reboot_path))
+        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(self.apply_path))
+        # An unarmed plan must not be installed automatically by the runner.
+        self.assertEqual(self.run_without_installation(), 0)
+        self.assertTrue(self.prepare())
+        self.assertTrue(os.path.isfile(self.apply_path))
+
+    def test_plan_unlink_failure_preserves_apply_marker(self):
+        self.existing_state()
+        before = {path: self.contents(path) for path in (
+            self.plan_path, self.apply_path, self.reboot_path)}
+        original_unlink = os.unlink
+
+        def unlink(path, *args, **kwargs):
+            if path == self.plan_path:
+                raise OSError("cannot remove plan")
+            return original_unlink(path, *args, **kwargs)
+
+        with patch.object(uu.os, "unlink", side_effect=unlink):
+            with self.assertRaises(OSError):
+                uu.consume_deferred_driver_plan(self.rootdir)
+
+        for path, contents in before.items():
+            self.assertEqual(self.contents(path), contents)
+
+    def test_directory_sync_failure_can_be_retried_without_installing(self):
+        self.existing_state()
+        with patch.object(uu.os, "fsync", side_effect=OSError):
+            with self.assertRaises(OSError):
+                uu.consume_deferred_driver_plan(self.rootdir)
+
+        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(self.plan_path))
+        self.assertTrue(os.path.isfile(self.apply_path))
+        # A second failed sync must still leave the retry marker intact.
+        with patch.object(uu.os, "fsync", side_effect=OSError):
+            self.assertEqual(self.run_without_installation(), 1)
+        self.assertTrue(os.path.isfile(self.apply_path))
+        self.assertEqual(self.run_without_installation(), 0)
+        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(self.apply_path))
+        self.assertEqual(self.contents(self.reboot_path), b"existing requirement\n")
+
+    def test_marker_unlink_failure_can_be_retried_without_installing(self):
+        self.existing_state()
+        original_unlink = os.unlink
+
+        def unlink(path, *args, **kwargs):
+            if path == self.apply_path:
+                raise OSError("cannot remove marker")
+            return original_unlink(path, *args, **kwargs)
+
+        with patch.object(uu.os, "unlink", side_effect=unlink):
+            with self.assertRaises(OSError):
+                uu.consume_deferred_driver_plan(self.rootdir)
+
+        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(self.plan_path))
+        self.assertTrue(os.path.isfile(self.apply_path))
+        self.assertEqual(self.run_without_installation(), 0)
+        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(self.apply_path))
+        self.assertEqual(self.contents(self.reboot_path), b"existing requirement\n")
+
+    def test_stale_marker_without_state_directory_is_cleared(self):
+        self.touch_marker(self.apply_path)
+        self.touch_marker(self.reboot_path)
+        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(os.path.dirname(self.plan_path)))
+
+        self.assertEqual(self.run_without_installation(), 0)
+
+        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(self.apply_path))
+        self.assertEqual(self.contents(self.reboot_path), b"existing requirement\n")
+
+    def test_corrupt_plan_is_not_treated_as_absent(self):
+        self.existing_state()
+        with open(self.plan_path, "w") as fp:
+            fp.write("{invalid json")
+
+        self.assertEqual(self.run_without_installation(), 1)
+
+        self.assertEqual(self.contents(self.plan_path), b"{invalid json")
+        self.assertTrue(os.path.isfile(self.apply_path))
+        self.assertEqual(self.contents(self.reboot_path), b"existing requirement\n")
+
+    def test_consumption_is_idempotent_and_preserves_reboot_requirement(self):
+        self.existing_state()
+
+        uu.consume_deferred_driver_plan(self.rootdir)
+        uu.consume_deferred_driver_plan(self.rootdir)
+
+        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(self.plan_path))
+        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(self.apply_path))
+        self.assertEqual(self.contents(self.reboot_path), b"existing requirement\n")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+#!/usr/bin/python3
+
+import signal
+import unittest
+from threading import Event
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import Mock, patch
+
+from test.test_driver_deferral_shutdown import shutdown
+
+
+class PollingFinished(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+class TestShutdownPolling(unittest.TestCase):
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.handler = object.__new__(shutdown.UnattendedUpgradesShutdown)
+        self.handler.options = SimpleNamespace(
+            wait_for_signal=True, stop_only=False, lock_file="test-lock")
+        self.handler.stop_signal_received = Event()
+        self.handler.wait_period = 0
+        self.handler.max_delay = 1800
+        self.handler.start_time = None
+        self.handler.iter_timer_set = False
+        self.handler.iteration_generation = 0
+        self.handler.shutdown_cancelled = False
+        self.handler.shutdown_pending = False
+        self.handler.lock_was_taken = False
+        self.handler.signal_sent = False
+        self.handler.on_shutdown_mode = None
+        self.handler.on_shutdown_mode_uu_proc = None
+        self.handler.apt_pkg_reinit_done = True
+        self.handler.get_logind_proxy = Mock()
+        self.properties = Mock()
+        self.process = Mock()
+        self.process.poll.return_value = None
+
+        self.glib = Mock()
+        self.add_patch(shutdown, "GLib", self.glib, create=True)
+        self.add_patch(shutdown.dbus, "Interface", Mock(return_value=self.properties))
+        self.add_patch(shutdown.signal, "signal", Mock())
+        self.add_patch(shutdown.time, "sleep", Mock())
+        self.add_patch(shutdown.os, "close", Mock())
+        self.add_patch(shutdown.os.path, "isfile", Mock(return_value=True))
+        self.add_patch(shutdown.apt_pkg, "get_lock", Mock(return_value=42))
+        self.stop_upgrade = Mock()
+        self.add_patch(shutdown, "signal_stop_unattended_upgrade", self.stop_upgrade)
+        self.popen = Mock(return_value=self.process)
+        self.add_patch(shutdown.subprocess, "Popen", self.popen)
+        for name in ("log_msg", "log_progress", "exit_log_result"):
+            self.add_patch(shutdown, name, Mock())
+
+    def add_patch(self, target, name, value, create=False):
+        patcher = patch.object(target, name, value, create=create)
+        patcher.start()
+        self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)
+
+    def poll_states(self, states, through_run=False):
+        samples = iter(states)
+
+        def get_state(*args):
+            try:
+                sample = next(samples)
+            except StopIteration:
+                raise PollingFinished()
+            if callable(sample):
+                sample = sample()
+            if isinstance(sample, Exception):
+                raise sample
+            return sample
+
+        self.properties.Get.side_effect = get_state
+        with self.assertRaises(PollingFinished):
+            if through_run:
+                self.handler.run()
+            else:
+                self.handler.run_polling(Mock())
+        self.assertFalse(self.handler.polling)
+        self.glib.timeout_add.assert_not_called()
+
+    def test_polling_continues_while_iteration_requests_monitoring(self):
+        self.handler.options.wait_for_signal = False
+        self.handler.iter = Mock(side_effect=[True, True, False])
+
+        self.handler.run_polling(Mock())
+
+        self.assertEqual(self.handler.iter.call_count, 3)
+        self.properties.Get.assert_not_called()
+
+    def test_polling_observes_cancellation_and_keeps_monitoring_child(self):
+        self.poll_states([True, False, False])
+
+        self.popen.assert_called_once()
+        self.process.send_signal.assert_called_once_with(signal.SIGTERM)
+        self.assertTrue(self.handler.shutdown_cancelled)
+        self.assertIs(self.handler.on_shutdown_mode_uu_proc, self.process)
+
+    def test_polling_without_glib_observes_cancellation(self):
+        with patch.dict(shutdown.__dict__):
+            shutdown.__dict__.pop("GLib", None)
+            self.poll_states([True, False, False], through_run=True)
+
+        self.popen.assert_called_once()
+        self.process.send_signal.assert_called_once_with(signal.SIGTERM)
+
+    def test_new_shutdown_waits_for_cancelled_child(self):
+        second_process = Mock()
+        second_process.poll.return_value = None
+        self.popen.side_effect = [self.process, second_process]
+
+        def old_child_finishes():
+            self.popen.assert_called_once()
+            self.process.poll.return_value = 0
+            return True
+
+        self.poll_states([True, False, True, old_child_finishes, True])
+
+        self.assertEqual(self.popen.call_count, 2)
+        self.assertIs(self.handler.on_shutdown_mode_uu_proc, second_process)
+        self.assertFalse(self.handler.shutdown_cancelled)
+

+        self.poll_states([True, False, False])
+
+        self.stop_upgrade.assert_called_once_with()
+        self.popen.assert_not_called()
+        self.assertFalse(self.handler.lock_was_taken)
+        self.assertFalse(self.handler.shutdown_pending)
+
+    def test_failed_property_read_does_not_mean_cancellation(self):
+        self.poll_states([
+            True, shutdown.dbus.exceptions.DBusException("temporary failure"),
+            True,
+        ])
+
+        self.popen.assert_called_once()
+        self.process.send_signal.assert_not_called()
+        self.assertTrue(self.handler.shutdown_pending)
+
+    def test_service_stop_while_waiting_never_launches_upgrade(self):
+        self.handler.stop_signal_received.set()
+
+        with self.assertRaises(SystemExit) as result:
+            self.handler.run_polling(Mock())
+
+        self.assertEqual(result.exception.code, 0)
+        self.properties.Get.assert_not_called()
+        self.popen.assert_not_called()
+
+    def test_cancellation_retains_child_monitoring_past_shutdown_deadline(self):
+        self.handler.shutdown_cancelled = True
+        self.handler.on_shutdown_mode_uu_proc = self.process
+        self.handler.start_time = 0
+        self.handler.max_delay = 1
+
+        with patch.object(shutdown.time, "time", return_value=100):
+            self.assertTrue(self.handler.iter())
+            self.handler.stop_signal_received.set()
+            with self.assertRaises(SystemExit) as result:
+                self.handler.iter()
+
+        self.assertEqual(result.exception.code, 1)
+        self.assertIs(self.handler.on_shutdown_mode_uu_proc, self.process)
+        self.process.kill.assert_not_called()
+        self.popen.assert_not_called()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
